title: KMS Forensics & Continuous Evidence Export Spec
body:
Purpose:
This working spec describes a continuous evidence export design and operational playbook focused on KMS/HSM/BYOK forensics, RBAC v2 key-access audit mapping, and SIEM ingestion. The goal is to provide engineers and auditors with a pragmatic pipeline that captures cryptographic control events, guarantees tamper-evident delivery to our SIEM/archive, and supports fast incident triage and cryptographic forensics.

Scope and context:
- Systems: Redwood-hosted KMS service, HSM appliances (cloud HSM + on-prem HSM), BYOK onboarding endpoints and key escrow store.
- Events: Key lifecycle events (create, import, rotate, disable, destroy), key-use events (decrypt, sign, wrap/unwrap), separation-of-duty operations (delegate, revoke, escrow retrieve), HSM firmware/slot events.
- Consumers: Security team (forensics + alerts), SRE (operational health), Compliance (evidence exports for audits), Privacy/Legal when keys relate to regulated data.
- Excludes: Application-level plaintext handling, token-level API usage that is unrelated to key management.

Design principles (quick):
1) Immutable evidence stream: events must be append-only, signed, and checksumed prior to leaving the source.
2) RBAC v2 linkage: every event must record the RBAC v2 subject and policy snapshot used to authorize the action.
3) Low-latency alerting + long-term archival: near-real-time SIEM ingestion for detection and a separate WORM store for audit retention.
4) Test-first ops: rotation canaries + synthetic forensic traces for every run to validate pipeline integrity before rotation completes.

High-level pipeline:
1) Event emission (KMS/HSM): KMS runtime emits canonical audit records for all key ops. HSM appliances emit syslog/OPAQUE events mapped into canonical format via an agent.
2) Local agent (collector): edge collector receives events, performs local signing with an evidence signing key (rotate this key via a separate governance flow), attaches a SHA256 digest, persists to local disk queue.
3) Forwarder: batched, idempotent upload to Kafka (internal) and concurrently to S3 WORM bucket as ndjson files for redundancy.
4) SIEM adapter: stream consumer transforms canonical events into Splunk/Datadog/QRadar formats and pushes with guaranteed-at-least-once semantics.
5) Archive + Search: downstream indexers for quick search; separate immutable store for auditor exports (retention policy applied).

RBAC v2 mapping requirements (per event):
- rbac_subject_id: principal id (user/service) performing the action.
- rbac_subject_type: user | service_account | approval_workflow | third_party_connector.
- rbac_policy_snapshot_id: immutable snapshot id capturing the policy state used to evaluate the request. (Policy snapshots kept for 7+ years; compressed.)
- rbac_evaluation_outcome: allow | deny | conditional_allow (with constraints captured).
- rbac_evaluation_reason: short string (e.g., matched-policy:admin-key-management OR matched-role:rotation-runner)

Canonical audit record (ndjson line example) — include in outputs exactly as part of archived evidence:
{"timestamp":"2025-11-12T18:23:45.123Z","event_id":"evt_1a2b3c","source":"kms-service","event_type":"key.rotate","key_id":"key_123","actor":"svc-rotate-01","rbac_subject_id":"svc-rotate-01","rbac_subject_type":"service_account","rbac_policy_snapshot_id":"pshot_20251112_01","rbac_evaluation_outcome":"allow","additional_context":"rotation-canary:pass","hsm_slot_id":"hsm-us-east-3:slot-7","evidence_signature":"MEUCIQ...","sha256":"b1946ac92492d2347c6235b4d2611184"}

Note: the JSON above is a single ndjson line; archived files are concatenations of such lines with monotonically increasing file suffixes.

Evidence signing and key hierarchy:
- Evidence Signing Key (ESK): dedicated keypair (HSM-protected) used by local collectors to sign batches. The ESK is rotated monthly and its rotation events are logged and archived.
- Evidence Key Escrow: ESK private keys are never exported except under multi-party approval (M-of-N) for emergency recovery. Escrow retrieval events are auditable and recorded by the collector.
- Chain of custody: each archived file contains metadata fields chain_prev_digest and chain_index to create an immutable chain across files for quick tamper detection.

SIEM export mapping notes:
- Splunk: map timestamp->_time, event_type->event_type, rbac_* fields as top-level fields, evidence_signature as evid_sig.
- Datadog: send as log event + facets for key_id, actor, rbac_evaluation_outcome. Use tags for hsm_slot_id and region.
- QRadar: translate to LEEF/CEF with event_id and event_type, include sha256 as payload hash.
- Add a consistent field: evidence_file_id for any artifact stored to the WORM archive so that SIEM alerts can link back.

Operational runbooks (short):
- Routine rotation (monthly): run rotation pipeline in canary mode for subset of non-prod keys. Verify synthetic evidence for each step. Promote to full rollout only after canary evidence is validated (hash chain intact + SIEM ingestion observed).
- Emergency key compromise: 1) Orchestrate key disable via KMS API, 2) trigger immediate evidence export job with high-priority routing, 3) notify PagerDuty and compliance queue with evidence_file_id and ESK signature.
- Evidence audit request: provide pre-authorized auditors with readonly signed ndjson bundle URLs + signed manifest. Use internal signed pre-signed URLs with 7-day access window.

Test harness and canary strategy (practical):
- Synthetic traces: for each rotation job we also emit a synthetic key.use event signed with a test-subject identity. This proves the end-to-end chain for that run.
- Chaos tests: simulate collector drops and verify forwarder replays recover sequence.
- Integrity checks: nightly job recomputes chain hashes and compares to recorded digest; any mismatch triggers an investigation ticket automatically created and notifies security-on-call.

Retention and compliance windows:
- Near-term SIEM: 1 year hot index (security team analytics).
- Audit archive (WORM): 7 years for regulated customers; 10 years for encryption keys tied to financial PII.
- Short-term dev test artifacts: 90 days and a separate flag to mark non-production bundles.

BYOK onboarding specifics (evidence-focused):
- During BYOK registration, collect the supplied key metadata (owner, purpose, allowed-regions) and store as an initial signed evidence artifact.
- Mandate automated policy snapshot capture at time-of-onboard; this snapshot becomes the policy anchor for all subsequent key-use events.
- BYOK emergency escrow retrieval must route through M-of-N approval and produce a dedicated evidence bundle with approver identities and timestamps.

Checklist (quick actionable items):
- [ ] Define canonical event schema versioning strategy (v1, v2...).
- [ ] Implement collector local signing with HSM-backed ESK.
- [ ] Create automation to snapshot RBAC v2 policy state per change and retain snapshots for retention window.
- [ ] Build SIEM transformers for Splunk/Datadog/QRadar.
- [ ] Add synthetic trace generation to rotation runner.
- [ ] Wire nightly integrity verifier and PagerDuty alerts.

Open questions / unresolved items (notes to self):
- Should evidence_file_id be UUIDv4 or deterministic (hash of first file chunk)? Tradeoffs: deterministic aids dedup; UUID avoids collision reasoning.
- How do we best represent conditional_allow in the RBAC snapshot when multiple constraints (time, IP, approval) exist? Do we include the constraint objects in-line or a reference id?
- Retention costs for long-lived archives: consider tiered cold storage and legal hold flags per-customer.

References and quick links:
- Confluence KMS design (linked above)
- HSM vendor guides (internal links in Confluence)
- Prior rotation incidents: SEC-INC-2024-07 (postmortem)

Notes to reviewers:
- This document is intentionally procedural and contains implementation hints that should map to a collector repo and rotation-runner code. Feedback wanted on schema fields and the M-of-N escrow flow language.
- If we agree on the canonical schema, I will draft a small ndjson generator and a Splunk ingestion spec as follow-ups.

-- Aisha
